I don't have any notes for you yet. My first attempt to open the sources failed because the research tool said I had no calls left, so I couldn't open any pages. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a link for each point, and not to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written commentary from memory.

Here is what I'll read for each part when I can run it again:

**1. Traditional verse-by-verse reading:**
- enduringword.com/bible-commentary/hosea-11/
- biblehub.com commentaries on Hosea 11 by Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary
- preceptaustin.org's Hosea 11 commentary

**2. Where Protestant traditions differ:**
- **v. 1**, quoted in Matthew 2:15 ("out of Egypt I called My son"): how prophecy and its fulfilment are read. Sources: Ligonier, Desiring God, The Gospel Coalition and Got Questions.
- **vv. 8–9**, God's compassion and "I am God and not man": what this says about God's feelings and his holiness. Sources: Wesley's Notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Spurgeon sermons on Hosea 11:4 and 11:8, and Lutheran sources (lcms.org, 1517.org).

**3. Other views:**
- **Modern scholarship:** the NET Bible notes, especially on the Hebrew text problems in vv. 4, 7 and 12. Also anything bibleodyssey.org has on God as a parent in Hosea.
- **Catholic and Orthodox:** the Church Fathers on v. 1 and Matthew 2:15 (newadvent.org), plus catholic.com and oca.org.
- **Popular modern teaching** (prosperity, word of faith, hyper-grace): only if the allowed sites actually discuss this chapter.

If you send a short message such as "continue", I'll start the research and give you the notes verse by verse with a link after each point.
